organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Transformed in Sudan into an international organization; set up training camps; by 1996 had cooperative ties with at least 20 Sunni extremist groups; took over training camps in Afghanistan after 1996.

organizations.name: National Islamic Front
organizations.notes: Seized power in a 1989 coup; welcomed al-Qa'ida and other extremist groups; led by Turabi.

organizations.name: Popular Arab and Islamic Conference
organizations.notes: Formed 1991 by Turabi as public face of outreach; attendees included PLO, HAMAS, Hizballah, and Iraqi, Afghan, Libyan and Iranian government representatives; dissolved 2000.

organizations.name: Iraqi intelligence
organizations.notes: Contacts with al-Qa'ida in Sudan; reported explosives training.

organizations.name: Islamic Movement of Iraqi Kurdistan
organizations.notes: Iraqi Kurdish group supported through Iraqi members of al-Qa'ida.

organizations.name: Shifa Pharmaceutical Plant
organizations.notes: Destroyed by US strikes in Aug 1998; reported links to Bin Ladin and Iraq.

key_claims: Al-Qa'ida was transformed in Sudan 1992-96 from a partly realized idea into an international organization able to operate independently.
Turabi's NIF welcomed al-Qa'ida to raise money, develop recruits, provide intelligence cover and advance its Islamist agenda.
By 1996 al-Qa'ida had cooperative ties with at least 20 Sunni extremist groups, and supported operations by at least eight before 1996.
Contacts between Iraq and al-Qa'ida in Sudan culminated in reported Iraqi explosives training for al-Qa'ida.
Al-Qa'ida took over almost all Afghan training camps on returning in 1996 and refocused them on terrorist tactics.
Sudan-era contacts may help al-Qa'ida compensate for the loss of its Afghan safehaven.
